untested_model.title: Untested scale model
untested_model.description: The {name} hasn't been tested with this integration yet. It belongs to the same family as the tested BF450, so it should work, but some readings or features may not. Please report how it works on the project's issue tracker. Setting up the scale doesn't connect to it; scale users are added afterwards.

user.description: Choose a Beurer scale that Home Assistant has seen nearby. Step on the scale to wake it if it isn't listed.

data_description.address: Scales Home Assistant has heard recently that aren't set up yet, with their Bluetooth address.

abort.already_configured: This scale is already set up.
abort.already_in_progress: This scale is already being set up.
abort.no_devices_found: No unconfigured Beurer scale has been seen nearby. Step on the scale to wake it, then try again.

create.title: Create new scale user
create.description: Home Assistant creates the scale user on the scale and chooses its consent code itself. The scale uses the profile to compute body composition.

data_description.person: Optional. Links the scale user to a Home Assistant person.
data_description.name: Leave empty to use the person's name.
data_description.birth_date: The scale supports ages from 10 to 100 years.

teach_more.title: Teach the scale
teach_more.description: Reading {reading} of {readings} taken. Each reading teaches the scale the new scale user's weight, so it recognises them afterwards. Step off and on again for another reading, or finish now.

adopt.title: Adopt existing slot
adopt.description: Use a slot whose consent code you know, for example one Home Assistant created before a reinstall. Don't adopt a scale user that the Beurer app also uses: Home Assistant must be its only client.

data_description.person: Optional. Links the scale user to a Home Assistant person.
data_description.name: Leave empty to use the person's name.
data_description.slot: The slot number on the scale.
data_description.consent_code: The 4-digit code chosen when this scale user was created.

reconfigure.title: Change scale user
reconfigure.description: Renaming the scale user or changing its person doesn't need the scale. Changing the profile does: Home Assistant then asks you to wake the scale and writes the new profile to it.

data_description.person: Optional. Links the scale user to a Home Assistant person.
data_description.name: Leave empty to use the person's name.
data_description.birth_date: The scale supports ages from 10 to 100 years.

repair_adopt.title: Enter the consent code again
repair_adopt.description: The scale rejected the consent code of {name} (slot {slot}). Enter the code this scale user was created with. Home Assistant checks it at the next wake.

data_description.consent_code: The 4-digit code chosen when this scale user was created.

repair_create.title: Create the scale user again
repair_create.description: Home Assistant creates {name} on the scale again, with the stored profile and a new consent code. The scale may put the scale user into a different slot; its sensors stay the same. Afterwards, {name} steps off and on the scale a few times so it learns to recognise them.

progress.wake: Step on the scale to wake it. Home Assistant then connects, checks the consent code and reads the profile from the scale.
progress.create: Step on the scale to wake it. Home Assistant then connects, creates the scale user on the scale and writes its profile.
progress.teach: Now the new scale user steps off the scale and on again: reading {reading} of {readings}. Stand still until the scale shows the result.
progress.reconfigure: Step on the scale to wake it. Home Assistant then connects and writes the new profile to the scale.

create_entry.teaching_timeout: Teaching ended because the scale got no further reading in time. The scale user was created with the readings taken so far.

error.name_required: Choose a person or enter a name.
error.name_in_use: Another scale user of this scale already has this name.
error.slot_in_use: This slot already is a scale user of this scale.
error.slot_not_found: The scale has no scale user in this slot.
error.invalid_consent_code: The scale rejected this consent code.
error.invalid_birth_date: Enter a birth date for an age between 10 and 100 years.

abort.no_free_slot: Every slot on the scale is taken. Remove a scale user first, then try again.
abort.wake_timeout: The scale didn't wake up within 3 minutes. Start again and step on the scale.
abort.pairing_unsupported: The Bluetooth adapter or proxy that reached the scale can't pair with it. Use an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy, or make the host adapter pairable.
abort.cannot_connect: Home Assistant couldn't talk to the scale. Make sure it is in range, then try again.
abort.teaching_timeout: Nobody stepped on the scale for the first teaching reading. The new scale user was removed from the scale again; start again to create it.
abort.consent_rejected: The scale rejected this scale user's consent code, so the profile couldn't be written. Nothing was changed.
abort.slot_now_empty: The scale no longer has a scale user in this slot. Open the repair again and choose to create the scale user again.
abort.profile_unknown: Home Assistant doesn't know this scale user's full profile, so it can't create it again. Remove the scale user and add it anew.
abort.slot_held_by_other_scale_user: The scale put the new scale user into a slot that another scale user of this scale still holds in Home Assistant, so Home Assistant removed it again. Repair or remove that scale user first.

pairing_impossible.title: {name} can't pair through this Bluetooth path
pairing_impossible.description:
Home Assistant reached the scale {name}, but the Bluetooth adapter or proxy it used couldn't pair (bond) with it. The scale only stays connected when it is paired, so readings aren't synced.

To fix it, do one of these:
- Add an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy on an ESP32 near the scale. ESPHome proxies pair with the scale automatically.
- If Home Assistant uses its own Bluetooth adapter, make the host adapter pairable. A local adapter on Home Assistant OS usually can't pair.

This issue goes away after the next successful sync.

unsupported_unit.title: {name} reports weights in {unit}
unsupported_unit.description:
The scale {name} sent readings in {unit} instead of kg. Home Assistant only supports kg and didn't record these readings, so your sensors don't show wrong values.

Set the scale's display unit back to kg, for example in the Beurer app. Home Assistant never changes the scale's settings. This warning goes away with the next reading in kg.

init.title: Fix {name}
init.description: The scale still has a scale user in this slot, but it rejects the consent code Home Assistant stored, for example because another client created a new scale user there. Home Assistant doesn't sync {name} until this is fixed.
